page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v6 is an x86_64 virtual machine from the Edsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 1 physical core and 2 dedicated vCPUs via hyperthreading. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 472 GB temporary disk, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPUs are included.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. Single-core performance is a strength, with Geekbench single-core scores of 2156.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 31.32 GB/sec ranking in the strong tier. However, multi-core and memory throughput benchmarks show significant limitations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 1991.98 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2649.0 are categorized as poor and weak, respectively, reflecting the physical single-core constraint. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 21.49 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.14 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarks.

Given the high memory density of 64 GB RAM paired with only 2 vCPUs, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. It is well-suited for small-scale databases, caching layers like Redis, or memory-intensive data processing tasks with low CPU concurrency. However, it is poorly suited for highly parallelized tasks, software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded workloads due to its single physical core limitation.
